For one due occurrence, failing and competing attempts leave exactly one effect and one receipt, holding the original due time and the later actual opening. Cases: a failure between effect and receipt leaves neither; a competing attempt that finds the LO busy gets nothing and is counted against no consumer; the completing attempt records one linked effect and receipt; a replay and the landed catch-up add nothing; storage refuses a second receipt for the same occurrence. Text from an unknown refusal is kept in no record and no return. A late claim to have opened the effect is refused by storage. Added in T1a-R2: an attempt that finds a row of its claim held by another connection (an office holder's identity) ends at once with a busy skip, no effect and no receipt, charged to no consumer.

A successful, confirmed, signed-in request opens at most one due item in its own LO after its response closes, and nothing else does. Cases, each through the real middleware and a real response close: the host switch off; a refusal the view handled; a marked request the view did not confirm; a later confirmed request that touches no LO; a session the landed gate turns away; the opening, with nothing opened inside the request and exactly one after its close; the same with Django's own connection cleanup running first; an attempt that finds its connection inside a transaction.

Each wake checks one consumer and opens at most one item, every consumer makes progress, and a failing item does not hold back the rest or lose its due time. Cases: a consumer whose selection fails is recorded and passed, so the next consumer runs; a CQ act refused at commit by the landed deferred completeness check leaves no act and no receipt; its valid sibling then opens; the refused occurrence opens later with its original due time; a late repair of an old failure does not disturb newer progress. Added in T1a-5b: a third thread past its Clarity response deadline opens on the consumer's next turn, so one consumer opens two purposes in due order; of two items due at the same instant, one that fails does not hold back the other; the CQ service's public entry for rule acts refuses any other operation and uses the connection it is named.

Work held by a Board Chair whose own term has a fixed end is held for the Board from that end, by the clock: nobody acts at that moment, the engine records the term end dated at the end, and that record's own commit moves the work. Cases: while another connection holds the activity the engine ends at once with nothing; once it is free the engine records exactly one term end, one receipt and one custody move, dated at the term's end; the landed catch-up then finds nothing more.

OD-2. Work that came back to a Chair by an automatic return is held when that Chair's term ends, even if a successor takes office at that same moment: asked about that instant, the landed function gives no holder and no office, and the projection shows the Chair holding the work until the handover and nobody from it.

Work the Board recovers after a dated mandate has ended early is held until the recovered officer's own ending, not until the mandate's nominal date (OD-1). The recorded custody shows the work held at the early end and recovered as its successor before the nominal date; asked at a late cut, the landed date function gives the officer's own deadline for the recovered spell and the nominal date for the spell that began while the mandate was live; the engine's selector offers no dated-end marker for the ended mandate.

The engine's measures are read across LOs by a current member of INTEVIA's Technology Circle, and by nobody else. Cases: the root's founder, holding a place in the Technology Circle the root's own birth batch names, reads counts for an ordinary LO's opening; nothing returned names an LO, a source or an effect; a member of the root with no place in that Circle, and a member of an ordinary LO, each get the one unavailable answer. T1a-R4b: an inactive credential, a restricted identity and a credential with no identity each get the same one unavailable answer.

The engine runs under one fixed version of its limits, and storage accepts no other. Cases: the version in force is exactly the ruled one and is the one the runner supports; a second version, a changed limit, and a version under another rule id are each refused by storage by name; the version in force is unchanged.

An attempt whose carrier is no longer the person who made the request, or whose act the writer refuses by name, leaves no effect and no receipt, and is recorded by its class. Cases: a wake carrying an access epoch that is no longer the person's ends as not eligible, before any consumer is probed, and is counted as a skip against the LO; a refusal the writer is known to give is reported and kept as that domain refusal, by its code, with the probe; the occurrence is then opened by the next clean attempt. T1a-9b: an occurrence the landed route completed after it was selected is found done through a whole attempt, with one receipt citing the landed effect and its earlier time, counted as found done.

An effect is "made here" only for the top-level transaction that wrote it, whichever savepoint of it wrote it, and for no other transaction, earlier, later or concurrent. Cases: a rolled-back savepoint leaves no effect and no origin; a top-level write is made here and is history after commit; a write in a released savepoint is made here and its commit passes the landed recovery guard; another session's write is unseen while uncommitted and not made here once committed; a full transaction id equal in its low 32 bits only is another transaction; an origin cannot be written directly, changed or removed.
